evidence: 0087 ports items 2-4 of main's 0066 (eb9b1ca; first 3490809). Patients can revoke a grant they gave (patient-approved or PIN-derived; never break-glass or workforce) through identity.revoke_my_consent_grant, bound to the live patient session. It serializes with the PIN commands on the PIN advisory key, writes one audit row whose reason is the fixed 'Revoked by the patient' (the patient's own words stay on the grant row, which no service reads, so the facility's audit readers never see them), and answers a replay idempotently. The access history labels breakGlass and revocableByPatient, which Identity publishes as patientRevocable; its limit of 50 now keeps the grants the patient can revoke and lists the chosen items newest first, the same list as 0030's for 50 grants or fewer. The inbox skips a deleted login. Preconditions pin the two replaced bodies (md5 ca6c848749f55e08a5f7a0a60c838293, 662353fa2a411879e4e8d869d54827d5), four relied-upon bodies, four CHECKs and the single probation trigger. 0087's only table lock is a momentary ACCESS SHARE on identity.consent_grants, taken by pg_get_constraintdef in a precondition and by the PL/pgSQL validator resolving the revoke's %rowtype, each released at once (measured: with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held on every other table 0087 applies without waiting; with it held on identity.consent_grants the apply stops on lock_timeout with nothing applied). ACCESS SHARE conflicts only with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, so no request waits for 0087, and it never locks platform.control_settings, so 0086's NOWAIT rule does not apply.
